column1: # Files and folders functions. One row per function, per task it belongs to. Tab-separated; see finder.py for the rules.

column7: summary
Reads a whole file as UTF-8 text into a string, or fails if it cannot be read.
Reads a file's lines into an Array, without their line endings; returns the count.
Reads a whole file into an Array of bytes; returns the number read.
Writes a string to a file as UTF-8, creating the file or replacing it.
Writes an Array of bytes to a file, creating the file or replacing it.
Adds text to the end of a file, creating the file if it is not there.
Adds an Array of bytes to the end of a file, creating the file if it is not there.
Replaces a file so a reader sees the old or the new contents, never a half-written file.
Returns true if a file or folder is there; false also when access is denied.
Returns true if the path is a file, following links; false if it cannot tell.
Returns true if the path is a folder, following links; false if it cannot tell.
Returns true if the path itself is a symbolic link.
Returns whether a path exists, or fails when it cannot tell, as when access is denied.
Joins two to four path parts with one separator; an absolute part drops those before it.
Returns the path without its last part, or an empty string for a root.
Returns the last part of a path, the file name, or an empty string for a root.
Returns the file name without its extension; a dotfile such as .gitignore keeps its name.
Returns the extension with its dot, such as .tiko, or an empty string if there is none.
Returns the file name up to its first dot, so a.tar.gz gives a.
Returns true if the file name has an extension; a dotfile has none.
Replaces a path's extension, or removes it when the new one is empty.
Adds an extension after any already there, so a.tar becomes a.tar.gz.
Splits a normalised path into its parts, without the root, in an Array; returns the count.
Returns the parts of a path as written, drive and root included, for a for each loop.
Holds one part of a path: its kind, such as root or parent, and its text.
Finds the next part of a path from an offset; returns a negative number when none is left.
Returns the root of a path, such as C:\ or /, or an empty string for a relative path.
Returns the length of a path's root, in characters.
Returns the platform's path separator: a backslash on Windows, a slash on Linux and macOS.
Returns a tidied path: . removed, .. resolved as text, duplicate separators collapsed.
Returns the path with the platform's separators, duplicates collapsed, nothing resolved.
Returns a path relative to a base folder; fails if the two have different roots.
Returns true if two paths match once normalised; case-insensitive on Windows.
Returns true if a path begins with another, comparing whole parts, not characters.
Returns true if a path needs no current folder; C:dev and \dev are not absolute.
Returns true if the whole path is just a root, such as C:\ or /.
Returns true if a relative path stays inside the folder it is joined to.
Returns true if a part of the path is a Windows device name such as CON or NUL.
Returns true if paths compare case-sensitively here: on Linux and macOS, not Windows.
Returns the full form of a path against the current folder; the path need not exist.
Returns the real path with links resolved; it must exist unless allowMissing is true.
Lists the entries of one folder for a for each loop; each entry may be a failure to check.
Lists every entry under a folder, subfolders included, for a for each loop.
Fills an Array with one folder's entries at once; returns the count.
Returns the entry's name, without its folder.
Returns the entry's full path, ready to open.
Returns how deep the entry is in a walk, 0 for the children of the folder walked.
Returns true if the entry is a file; a link reports as a link, not as its target.
Returns true if the entry is a folder; a link to a folder reports as a link.
Returns true if the entry is a symbolic link.
Returns true if the entry is a device, pipe or socket rather than a file, folder or link.
Returns the entry's FileInfo: free on Windows, one extra system call on Linux and macOS.
Copies a file; fails if the destination exists unless overwrite is true.
Moves or renames a file, even across volumes; refuses an existing destination by default.
Deletes a file; fails if it is not there.
Replaces one file with another in a single step, so the target is never missing.
Creates one folder; fails if something is already there.
Creates a folder and any missing parents; succeeds if it already exists.
Deletes an empty folder; fails if it still holds anything.
Deletes a folder and all it holds without following links; returns how many it removed.
Copies a folder and everything in it; returns how many entries it created.
Chooses whether CopyDir replaces files already at the destination; false by default.
Chooses whether CopyDir keeps each file's times; false by default.
Chooses whether CopyDir keeps permission bits or attributes; false by default.
Chooses whether CopyDir copies a link as a link rather than its target; true by default.
Returns the system's temporary folder; creates nothing.
Creates a uniquely named temporary file and returns its path; it is not deleted for you.
Creates a uniquely named temporary folder and returns its path; it is not deleted for you.
Returns the user's home folder, without a trailing separator.
Returns the folder for user settings, such as AppData\Roaming or ~/.config.
Returns the folder for user data files, such as AppData\Local or ~/.local/share.
Returns the folder for files that can be rebuilt, such as AppData\Local or ~/.cache.
Returns the folder for logs, history and recent files, such as ~/.local/state.
Returns the full path of the running program, however it was started.
Returns a path with a leading ~ replaced by the user's home folder.
Returns the program's current folder.
Changes the program's current folder, for every thread at once.
Returns a path's FileInfo, following symbolic links; fails if the path is missing.
Returns a path's FileInfo without following a symbolic link, so a link describes itself.
Returns true if the FileInfo describes something that exists.
Returns true if the path is a regular file.
Returns true if the path is a folder.
Returns true if the path is a symbolic link; only ever true from LStat.
Returns true if the path is a device, pipe or socket rather than a file, folder or link.
Returns the size in bytes.
Returns the last-write time as a chrono.Instant.
Returns the last-write time in ticks of 100 ns since 0001-01-01 UTC.
Returns the creation time as a chrono.Instant; check HasCreated first.
Returns the creation time in ticks, or 0 when HasCreated is false.
Returns the last-access time as a chrono.Instant; often not kept up to date.
Returns the last-access time in ticks, or 0 when HasAccessed is false.
Returns true if the platform records creation times, so Created means something.
Returns true if the platform records access times, so Accessed means something.
Returns true if unwritable: the read-only flag, or no write bit on Linux and macOS.
Returns true if hidden: the hidden flag on Windows, a leading dot on Linux and macOS.
Returns the raw attribute word: attributes on Windows, mode bits on Linux and macOS.
Returns the raw attribute word: attributes on Windows, mode bits on Linux and macOS.
Returns true if OwnerUid and OwnerGid are filled in: on Linux and macOS, not on Windows.
Returns the owner's user id, or 0 unless HasOwner is true.
Returns the owner's group id, or 0 unless HasOwner is true.
Opens a file on a file number for reading or writing text, bytes or records.
Returns an unused file number for Open, or 0 if all 255 are taken.
Closes one or more file numbers, or every open file when given none.
Closes every open file, or resets a redirected standard input or output stream.
Opens a text file for reading with Open; the file must already exist.
Opens a text file for writing with Open, creating it or emptying it first.
Opens a text file with Open to add to its end, creating the file if needed.
Opens a file with Open for reading and writing bytes at any position.
Opens a file with Open for reading and writing fixed-size records, 128 bytes by default.
Limits a Binary or Random file in Open to reading, writing, or both.
Opens a Binary or Random file for reading only, in an Access clause.
Opens a Binary or Random file for writing only; an existing file is emptied first.
Opens a Binary or Random file for both reading and writing, the default.
Sets the Unicode encoding of a text file in Open; a file read this way needs a BOM.
Writes values as text to an open file; a trailing comma or semicolon skips the line break.
Writes values to a file as comma-separated text, strings in quotes, for Input # to read.
Reads comma- or line-separated values from a text file into variables.
Reads one line of a text file into a string, without its line ending.
Reads a variable, string or array from a file as bytes, at a position or the current one.
Writes a variable, string or array to a file as bytes, at a position or the current one.
Returns true when an open file has nothing left to read.
Returns the length in bytes of an open file.
Returns where the last read or write happened in an open file, counted in records.
Returns the 1-based position of the next read or write: bytes, or records for Random.
Sets the 1-based position of the next read or write: bytes, or records for Random.
Restricts other programs' access to a record or byte range of an open file.
Removes a restriction that Lock put on a record or byte range.
Reads a file a line at a time in a for each loop, never holding the whole file in memory.
Holds a reader that decodes lines and text from any Stream, in UTF-8 or UTF-16.
Reads the next decoded line into a string; returns false at the end.
Appends all the remaining decoded text to a string.
Returns the encoding found at the start: utf-8, utf-16le or utf-16be.
Holds what a TextReader does with invalid UTF-8: replace it or fail.
Holds a writer that sends text to any Stream as UTF-8, with an optional BOM.
Writes a string followed by the writer's NewLine.
Holds an open file: a Stream over a handle it owns and closes when it goes out of scope.
Opens a file the way an OpenOptions says: read, write, append, create and more.
Opens an existing file for reading only.
Opens a file for writing, creating it or emptying it first.
Creates a new file for writing; fails if one is already there.
Opens a file so every write goes to its end, creating it if needed.
Creates and opens a new, randomly named file in a folder or the temporary folder.
Closes the file and reports any error the close itself raised.
Returns true if the File has a file open.
Returns the path the file was opened with.
Reads up to n bytes at an offset without moving the position.
Writes bytes at an offset without moving the position; refused in append mode.
Returns the open file's current size in bytes.
Truncates the file to a size, or extends it with zero bytes.
Forces the file's data and metadata onto the disk, so a write survives a power cut.
Forces the file's data onto the disk; can be cheaper than Sync on Linux.
Returns the open file's FileInfo, read from the handle even if the file was renamed.
Locks the whole file, waiting until it is free: exclusive by default, or shared.
Locks the whole file if it is free, or fails at once if another holder has it.
Releases this handle's lock; succeeds when none is held.
Returns the FileId of the open file, still right after a rename.
Returns the operating-system handle or descriptor, or -1 when closed.
Holds the flags that say how File.Open opens a file: read, write, create, share and more.
Returns the OpenOptions for reading a file that must already exist.
Returns the OpenOptions for writing a new file or an existing one emptied.
Returns the OpenOptions for adding to the end of a file, creating it if needed.
Holds a file of fixed-size records of one type, read and written by number.
Opens a file of records for reading and writing, creating it if it is missing.
Reads record n into a variable; false when the file has no such record.
Writes a variable as record n, growing the file when n is past the end.
Writes a variable after the last record and returns its record number.
Returns the number of whole records in the file.
Reads record n of a type from an open File, counting records from 1.
Writes a value as record n of an open File, growing the file if needed.
Returns the number of whole records of a type in an open File.
Holds the base type of every byte stream, with read, write, seek and flush.
Reads up to n bytes and returns how many; 0 means the end of the data.
Reads exactly n bytes, or fails if the data ends first.
Appends every remaining byte to an Array; returns how many.
Writes up to n bytes and returns how many it wrote, which may be fewer.
Writes all n bytes, calling Write as often as it takes.
Writes every byte of an Array.
Writes a string as UTF-8, with no BOM.
Writes a string in a text encoding, the bytes WriteAllText would write.
Moves the position from the start, the current place or the end; returns the new position.
Returns the current position, or fails on a stream that cannot seek.
Passes any buffered bytes on to where they are going.
Returns true if Read can succeed on this stream.
Returns true if Write can succeed on this stream.
Returns true if Seek can succeed on this stream.
Holds where Stream.Seek measures from: the start, the current position or the end.
Copies a stream from its position to its end into another; returns the byte count.
Holds a growable byte buffer in memory that reads, writes and seeks like a file.
Returns the number of bytes held, whatever the position.
Empties the stream; its length and position become 0.
Copies every byte held into an Array; returns the count.
Returns the bytes held decoded as text, the same way ReadAllText decodes a file.
Returns the bytes held decoded in a text encoding, as ReadAllText would read them.
Holds a Stream that reads another in large pieces, so many small reads stay fast.
Reads the next byte; returns false at the end.
Reads the next line as raw bytes in a string, not decoded; returns false at the end.
Appends bytes up to and including a delimiter to an Array; returns the count.
Copies up to n upcoming bytes into an Array without consuming them.
Holds a Stream that gathers small writes and passes them on in large pieces.
Fills an Array with the paths that match a wildcard pattern; returns the count.
Returns true if a string matches a wildcard pattern, without touching the disk.
Returns the folder a pattern search starts from: the part before the first wildcard.
Returns the offset of a pattern's first wildcard, or -1 if it has none.
Returns true if a pattern has a double-star part that searches every subfolder.
Limits how deep a walk goes: 1 is the immediate children, 0 (the default) no limit.
Chooses whether a walk enters linked folders; false by default, so it cannot loop.
Chooses whether a walk returns folders as well as files; true by default.
Chooses whether a walk returns hidden entries; true by default.
Chooses whether a walk ends at its first error; false by default, so it carries on.
Chooses whether a walk returns each folder after its contents; false by default.
Chooses whether a walk lists each folder in name order; false by default.
Sets a function that decides, entry by entry, what a walk returns and what it enters.
Holds the type of a walk filter: a function that says skip, yield, descend or stop.
Holds a walk filter's answer: skip, yield, descend into, or stop after an entry.
Skips the contents of the folder a walk has just returned.
Holds the iterator ReadDir hands out, for stepping through a folder without for each.
Holds the iterator WalkDir hands out, for stepping through a walk without for each.
Returns true while the iterator is on an entry.
Moves the iterator on to the next entry.
Returns the current entry by reference; the next MoveNext makes it invalid.
Returns the portable error code, such as FS_NOT_FOUND, to branch on.
Returns a fixed one-line description of the error code.
Returns the path the failed call was working on, or an empty string.
Returns the second path of a failed copy, move or link call.
Returns the operating system's own error number, or 0 if the library raised the error.
Returns the name of the call that failed, for diagnostics only.
Creates a symbolic link to a target; on Windows this usually needs privilege.
Gives an existing file a second name on the same volume.
Returns the target a symbolic link points to, as stored; fails if it is not a link.
Returns true if the path itself is a symbolic link.
Returns how many hard links, or names, a file has.
Returns the FileId of a path, which tells whether two paths are the same file.
Returns whether two paths name the same file; fails if either is missing.
Holds a volume and file number that are equal for every name of one file.
Sets or clears a file's read-only flag, or its write bits on Linux and macOS.
Sets or clears a file's hidden flag on Windows; fails as unsupported on Linux and macOS.
Returns a file's permission bits on Linux and macOS; fails as unsupported on Windows.
Sets a file's permission bits on Linux and macOS; fails as unsupported on Windows.
Returns a file's raw Windows attribute flags; fails as unsupported on Linux and macOS.
Replaces a file's whole Windows attribute word; fails as unsupported on Linux and macOS.
Sets a file's modified and accessed times; a time of 0 leaves that one alone.
Sets a symbolic link's own times, leaving its target alone.
Changes a file's owner and group on Linux and macOS, -1 keeping one; fails on Windows.
Changes a symbolic link's own owner and group, on Linux and macOS only.
Returns the total, free and available bytes of the volume a path is on.
Returns the capacity of the volume in bytes.
Returns the free bytes on the volume, ignoring quotas; the number to report.
Returns the bytes this user may still write; the number to check before writing.
Returns the VolumeInfo of the volume a path is on: its root, label and file system.
Fills an Array with a VolumeInfo for each drive or mounted disk; returns the count.
Returns where the volume is mounted, such as C:\ or /.
Returns the volume's label, which may be empty and always is on Linux and macOS.
Returns the file system's name, such as NTFS or ext4, or an empty string.
Returns the longest file or folder name the volume allows, not the longest path.
Returns true if the whole volume is read-only.
Returns true if names on this volume are case-sensitive.
Returns true if the volume can hold symbolic links; false is certain, true a best guess.
Takes a lock on a file that cooperating programs share, waiting up to a timeout.
Releases the lock; harmless when none is held.
Returns true while this FileLock holds its lock.
Maps a file into memory, read-only unless writable is true; an empty file fails.
Returns a pointer to the mapped bytes, valid until Close.
Returns the size of the mapped file in bytes.
Writes changed mapped bytes to the disk now.
Returns true while a file is mapped.
Unmaps the file; harmless when nothing is mapped.
Starts watching a folder for changes, subfolders too when recursive is true.
Fills an Array with the changes seen since the last call, waiting up to a timeout.
Stops watching; harmless when not watching.
Returns true while the watcher is running.
Returns what happened: created, deleted, modified, renamed, or overflow.
Returns the full path of the entry that changed.
Opens a serial port on a file number, with its speed, parity and other settings.
Opens standard input or output on a file number, to use like a file.
Opens standard input and standard error on a file number, to use like a file.
Opens a printer on a file number, so Print # and Put # send data to it.
Runs a shell command and opens its input or output on a file number.
Opens the screen on a file number, for reading and writing like a file.
Parses TOML text into a TomlValue tree whose root is a table, or a ConfigError.
Reads a UTF-8 TOML file into a TomlValue tree, or a ConfigError.
Holds one TOML value or table; look keys up with Get, Find or a dotted Path.
Returns a TomlValue table as TOML text; comments are not kept.
Parses INI text into an IniFile of sections and keys, or a ConfigError.
Reads an INI file into an IniFile, or a ConfigError.
Writes an IniFile to a file as INI text.
Holds an INI file's sections and keys in file order: Get, SetValue, Remove.
